answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may bid, with the bond sized to the value at risk. When an agent defaults or submits provably fraudulent work, a verifier can trigger slashing; reputation alone is not enough, since a newcomer can discard it. Sybils can still be created, but each must immobilize capital and risk losing it, so splitting one attacker across many umber, falcon, or ocean-named identities multiplies the cost rather than multiplying influence for free.
